raw_response:
I've been farming 5 years now, took over most of the land from my father when he got older and my brother went to work in Shijiazhuang. 163 mu is a lot to manage, especially when it's just me, my wife, and sometimes my parents helping out. I've got to be careful about where I put my money — that's a lot of fertilizer and pesticide bills every year.

**My thinking crop by crop:**

The wheat and maize on my 80 mu rotation fields — that's my bread and butter, literally. I know what I'm doing there. My neighbor Lao Zhang gets good wheat yields and he puts down about 50 kg of compound fertilizer as base before sowing, then tops up with about 25-30 kg urea at jointing. I do the same. For maize, I switched to Xianyu 335 three years ago because almost everyone around here uses it and yields are good. I put the compound fertilizer in at sowing and then throw on urea around big bell stage. I don't irrigate maize much — usually just once before sowing if soil is dry, and once at tasseling if it hasn't rained.

The broccoli and watermelon are cash crops on separate plots. I've been growing them 3 years. They need more irrigation and I use more fertilizer on them because the margins are better. An input dealer from the county town told me broccoli likes potassium, so I started adding more potash to those fields.

Stevia I started last year on 15 mu. My cousin in the next village grows it for a company that comes and collects the leaf. The price is stable and it doesn't need as much fussing as vegetables. I'll keep that going.

Chili I grow 15 mu — mostly sell fresh to local traders. It takes a lot of water and you have to watch for disease, especially in wet years. I spray more often than I used to because two years ago I lost a lot to anthracnose.

Cotton I've been reducing every year. The price is okay but the pest management is exhausting. 20 mu is enough — I know the routine and I can handle it myself.
